A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same 3DRS work. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, with retained tables, figures and passages matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original 3DRS benchmark results, correspondence analyses, ablations and qualitative examples across five scene-understanding datasets.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds VSI-Bench evaluation and appendix experiments on simultaneous multi-layer supervision and distillation losses.

M1.justification: The architecture and feature-alignment procedure are retained. V1 specifies cosine distillation; v2 describes Euclidean distillation and assigns the retained main scores to Euclidean loss in Table 13, but keeps the cosine formula and definition in Section 2.2.2. Whether this represents an actual method change or a reporting correction remains unresolved.

E1.justification: V2 retains the five original benchmarks and adds VSI-Bench. Its numerical and multiple-choice spatial tasks include distance estimation, object and room sizes, route planning and appearance order, substantially extending the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: The new VSI-Bench comparison introduces a substantially different comparator set, including GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5 Pro, LongVA-7B, InternVL2-40B and 72B LLaVA variants (v2 Table 2). Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds experimental configurations combining supervision of the last, third-last and fifth-last layers, and comparing Euclidean, cosine and combined losses (Tables 12–13). The stated frame count, optimizer, batch size and split descriptions for the original benchmarks are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds targeted analyses of whether supervising multiple layers helps and whether the distillation distance function matters. These supplement v1's existing teacher, supervision-signal and individual-layer ablations; the earlier analyses and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or formal significance tests for its experiments. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original comparison tables retain their numerical entries, while v2 adds substantial new results. Table 2 reports a VSI-Bench average of 45.9 for 3DRS and 45.4 for Gemini-1.5 Pro. Tables 12–13 add layer and loss comparisons; for example, ScanRefer Acc@0.25 is 62.9, 61.5 and 60.5 with one, two and three supervised layers.

T1.justification: The displayed correspondence definitions, loss equations and Appendix A.1 coordinate computation remain unchanged. Expanded motivation for correspondence analysis introduces no new derivation or proof. The conflicting loss description is an unresolved methodological reporting issue.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the central correspondence-quality and 3D-supervision claims. The conclusion softens v1's explicit claim to be the first such investigation to describing the area as largely unexplored, while the introduction expands the stated dataset scope from five to six.

C2.justification: V2 adds a specific limitation concerning propagation of teacher errors and biases, beyond the retained small-training-dataset limitation. Appendix A.4 suggests that simultaneous multi-layer supervision over-constrains geometry and weakens semantics, and interprets the loss comparison as showing limited sensitivity to distance-function choice.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly identifies VG-LLM pretraining data as the data used for the VSI-Bench experiment, although detailed preparation and training instructions are not supplied. Existing hardware, optimization settings, coordinate-processing information and the project-page disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 adds focused discussion of FiT3D and earlier 3D detection and representation-distillation work, including BEVDistill, Pri3D and OpenScene, distinguishing their settings from MLLMs. Section 2.1.2 also adds correspondence-related literature. These expand the context while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds 3DRS to the title, rewrites the conclusion and selected explanatory passages, moves the qualitative discussion into Appendix A.5, and promotes limitations to main-text Section 6. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 2, 12 and 13, relocates Figure 4 to the appendix, and changes Figure 3's label from Cosine Loss to Similarity Loss. Existing plots, qualitative examples and comparison-table structures are largely preserved, with renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful benchmark evidence, targeted ablations and explicit teacher-error limitations. However, its Euclidean-loss description and Table 13 conflict with the retained cosine formula, making the main results' training objective less clear than in v1. The new VSI-Bench discussion also claims leading appearance-order performance despite Table 2 showing 39.2 for 3DRS versus 48.6 for LLaVA-Video-72B. These benefits and reporting regressions leave the net quality change uncertain.
